body:
# oh-my-codex v0.22.6

## Summary

This patch release ships three fixes: team lock recovery preservation, cleanup logic that protects active temporary directories, and question terminal state preservation for reliable answer handling.

## Fixed

- **PRESERVE SHARED LOCKS DURING RECOVERY (#4075):** Team membership, scaling, task-claim, mailbox, and shared dispatch locks now preserve stale locks and report `team_lock_recovery_required` instead of deleting another operation's replacement lock. After a crash, confirm all users of the lock have stopped before manually removing the reported directory; automatic crash recovery is intentionally disabled.
- **PRESERVE ACTIVE TEMPORARY DIRECTORIES DURING CLEANUP (#4076):** `omx cleanup` now preserves temporary directories and only reaps orphaned OMX MCP processes. A directory name and modification time do not establish ownership, and matching temporary directories may contain active projects or uncommitted work.
- **PRESERVE THE FIRST TERMINAL QUESTION STATE (#4077):** A stale question UI, renderer replacement, or timeout handler could overwrite an accepted answer or report it as a failure. Question state transitions are now serialized and the first terminal state is preserved across API, UI, error, and supersede paths. Only the winning answer runs answer side effects; terminal records survive late submissions and cancellation.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Cargo workspace, and plugin metadata) all report `0.22.6`.

## Verification

- Full CI on dev candidate (candidate details recorded in [release readiness](docs/qa/release-readiness-0.22.6.md)).
- PR #4075 CI passed on its merged head.
- PR #4076 CI passed on its merged head.

name: v0.22.5
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.22.5

## Summary

This patch release ships two critical team runtime safety improvements: fail-closed task-read error handling and memory/secrets/API preservation across state mutations.

## Fixed

- **FAIL CLOSED ON TASK READS AND STALE REPLY TARGETS (#4067):** Team runtime now fails closed on task read failures, handling corrupted task files and unresolvable reply targets instead of silently ignoring them. This prevents task loss and state inconsistency during malformed or id-mismatched operations.
- **PRESERVE MEMORY WRITES, SECRETS, AND API AVAILABILITY (#4068):** Integration and worker operations now preserve memory writes, API availability state, and secret values across state mutations. Previous mutations could lose in-flight writes, reset API state during recovery, or drop configured secrets, causing workflows to restart or fail. This fix ensures state consistency across all operations.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Cargo workspace, and plugin metadata) all report `0.22.5`.

## Verification

- Full CI on dev candidate (candidate details recorded in [release readiness](docs/qa/release-readiness-0.22.5.md)).

name: v5.1.66
body:
**`omo thread` says when a broken install leaves it on this device only.** A thread client sidecar that cannot be loaded no longer makes `omo thread read <alias>` silently answer `not_found`: stderr names the sidecar, the error, and the reinstall step. The CLI sign-in's own warnings (a retired trust pin, a failed device-service forget) now reach stderr too. ([#12936](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12936))

**A message to a busy thread now reaches the turn it is running, by default.** `thread_send` and `thread_handoff` with no delivery mode (and `omo thread send` without `--mode`) steer the recipient's running turn and start a turn when it is idle, on this device and on another device alike; a message queues behind the running turn only when the caller asks for `follow_up`, or when the turn cannot take a steer (a waiting question, a compaction, an engine that reports no turn epoch). A send that steers a turn ending at that very moment falls back to the lane the target has then instead of failing. ([#12921](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12921), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9-2.** A tool that an eval cell awaits no longer leaves the running cell blank for a moment when it finishes: its streamed lines stay until the cell's own output or its result replaces them (senpi#6257). ([#12920](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12920))

**`omo remote send` now travels the same road as a session's `thread_send` to another device, and every reply from another device is explained by one mapping.** The person at a terminal who sends to a session on another device goes through the relay transport (the same offline check, the same steer preflight against the running turn, a receipt in this device's gateway store) while keeping their own prompt record; what the user reads when a command on another device is refused (`omo remote`, the attach TUI, the thread tools and the SDK) comes from a single module, so a device that did not answer, a missing grant or an uncertain result reads the same everywhere. ([#12911](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12911), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12885](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12885))

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.9.** It brings senpi's `admit_external_message` (a message relayed from another device's session is admitted as an ordinary delivery) and makes a relayed delivery read exactly like a same-machine one, with the device kept in its metadata only. The one-channel relay transport (#12879) needs both. ([#12904](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12904))

**The Install button on omo.dev's header no longer presses against or slips past the pill's right edge.** The floating nav bar gives its last control the same inset as the logo on the left, and below 1000 px the section links move into the menu so nothing is pushed outside the pill in any language. ([#12893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12893))

**A thread an agent creates or forks with `thread_create` now starts in the creator's own approval mode on this device too, not the host's default.** A session created on another device already did (#6189); the two legs now run one body: a name is checked against the device the thread lands on (a name that device already lists live is `name_conflict` there), opening a thread that is live on another device answers that thread without opening it again, and the created thread's facts (name, working directory, timestamps) come from the engine's reply on both devices. ([#12891](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12891), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**Stopping, closing, renaming, re-modelling, changing the reasoning level of, or reading a thread works the same way whether that thread runs on this machine or on another device of your account.** `thread_set_reasoning` now reaches a thread on another device too, and a session with no file yet that another client still holds answers the same on both. ([#12890](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12890), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message an agent sends to a session on another device now arrives there exactly as a message between sessions on one device.** The receiving session gets a delivery entry (never a user message) with the same sender line and authority notice a same-device delivery carries, deduplicated under the same key, and it wakes on receipt the same way; a reply is just another send back. Nothing in the delivered text names the device it crossed, and `omo remote send` from a terminal is unchanged. A send from `omo thread send` to a session on another device is refused as data (the engine admits a command-line delivery only from its own machine) and points at `omo remote send`. ([#12889](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12889), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879), fixes [#12882](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12882), fixes [#12877](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12877), fixes [#12346](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12346), fixes [#12865](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12865), fixes [#12857](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12857))

**Sending a message to another session now goes through one delivery pipeline whether that session is on this machine or on another device.** The device difference is a transport module behind one port; nothing a user sees changes in this release. ([#12887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12887), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879))

**A message to a session on another device now reads exactly like one from a session on the same machine.** The receiving agent sees which session sent it, not which device, and replies by that session as usual. ([#12878](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12878))

**A subagent whose model takes more than 90 s to start answering is no longer aborted by runtime fallback.** With `runtime_fallback` enabled, the first-prompt watchdog cut every subagent that showed no progress within a fixed 90 s and re-prompted the fallback model, so reasoning-heavy models that legitimately think longer before their first token were killed and their prompt was sent twice. The watchdog now waits 300 s, the same stream-start bound the engines use, and `runtime_fallback.first_prompt_timeout_seconds` sets it (`0` disables it). ([#11893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11893), fixes [#11887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11887))

### Fixed

- `omo thread send` to a thread alias held on this device now reaches that thread when run from another workspace, the same way `omo thread read` does, instead of answering that no visible thread matches. ([#12860](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12860))
- Memory shutdown drain: the session-shutdown wiring no longer claims senpi puts no bound on its handler. senpi bounds one `session_shutdown` handler with its own warn threshold, per-handler timeout and total quit budget (shipped defaults 2 s / 10 s / 2 s, each user-tunable and 0-disableable), and the 1500 ms drain budget is sized under those defaults and pinned by a test that reads them from the installed senpi, so a host release that lowers a default below the drain fails there. No host cap was added from OmO and nothing bypasses the host abort; a journal flush skipped by the budget still raises its error-level alarm. ([#12795](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12795), refs [#10336](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10336))
- The browser skill's docs and examples teach BrowserSkill 0.4 shared control for the omowright it now ships (`^0.3.0`): every gated page action carries the context of a fresh `session.cooperate("sync")`, and a `cooperation_sync_required` refusal waits for the person with `session.cooperate("wait")`, then re-syncs and replans. They also note which calls are gated, that a gated action throws a `TypeError` on an unknown option key (with the two calls that pass stray keys through instead), and that `page.on("dialog")` listeners receive a `Dialog` they can answer. The omowright this release ships includes running-browser discovery through `DevToolsActivePort`, `goto` on sparse and frameset pages, UTF-8 decoding across BrowserSkill IPC chunks and unique-only stale-ref recovery (thanks @ashmoonori-afk, code-yeongyu/omowright#115 to #118), and agent tabs in their own window (thanks @devxoul, code-yeongyu/omowright#120). ([#12494](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12494))
- The senpi-task cold-revive residency test is now bounded by the product's own liveness rules instead of a flat 20 s total (Part of #10993). A Windows child that blocks for a while during startup no longer fails it unless the product would also give up, and a real stall fails with the last stage it reached and the stall length. The test's child also reports senpi's startup phase timings, so the next block names its phase. ([#11706](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11706))

### Changed

- Skills: `ulw-research` and mass research in `mass-ulw` now require every conclusion to rest on something a tool actually observed. Workers tag claims `OBSERVED:` and dead ends `PROBED:`, anything known only from memory is sent back as a lead, and mass-research verify nodes re-open each observed source. Both research editions state the rule in their opening contract, and every mass-ulw node prompt carries it in its VERIFY item. ([#12832](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12832), fixes [#12830](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12830))

name: v2.2.7
body:
### Highlights

- **GitHub Copilot Auto**: Pick **Auto** in the model picker when your Copilot account has an Auto pool, and Copilot's router chooses the model for each session at the Auto discount. If routing fails, OpenCode falls back to the account's default chat model. ([#62997](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62997))
- **Side Panel Tab Shortcuts**: Right-click a side panel tab and choose **Close tabs to the right**. `⌘W` now closes side panel tabs wherever focus is, `⌥⌘W` or `Ctrl+Alt+W` always closes the session tab, and `⌘⇧T` reopens the last closed tab of either kind where it was. ([#62922](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62922))
- **Mark Sessions Read or Unread**: Open the menu on a tab, Home row, project row or inbox card and choose **Mark as unread** to keep its dot until you next visit. ([#62889](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62889))

### Breaking changes

#### `@opencode/ai`: `ImageResponse.image` is removed

This affects code that imports `@opencode/ai` directly. Read `response.images[0]` instead of `response.image`. ([#63011](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63011))

#### SDK: fewer endpoints wait for plugins to load

On a Location that is still loading plugins, `agent.list` returns the agents loaded so far, and `integration.list`, `usage.limits`, `vcs.init`, `rpc.call` and `artifact.*` no longer wait up to 5 seconds. Entries and actions that a plugin provides appear when it finishes loading, so refresh on the matching `*.updated` event. Model, provider, `generate.*`, `voice.*` and `websearch.query` endpoints still wait. ([#62796](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62796), [#63040](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63040))

### Core

#### Improvements

- **MCP Logins Stay Signed In**: Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer sign you out when several clients refresh at once or the token endpoint fails for a moment. ([#62827](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62827), [#63012](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63012))
- `read` accepts a negative `offset` to read from the end of a file, such as `-50` for the last 50 lines. An offset past the end returns the last lines and the file's line count instead of failing. ([#62147](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62147))
- When `read` can't find a file, it suggests close names: different capitalization, another extension, a small typo, or the matching path inside the project. ([#62147](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62147))
- Shell results end with `Exit code: N`. Commands killed by a signal show the signal name, and timeouts say how long they waited and suggest a larger timeout. ([#62141](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62141))
- Prompt cache warming times its pings from the model's `cache.ttl` by default (`interval: "auto"`), or every 4 minutes without a TTL. Models whose cache outlasts the warming `duration` are no longer pinged. ([#62831](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62831))
- When MCP servers connect, disconnect or change tools, Code Mode sends the model a short list of what changed instead of the whole tool catalog. ([#62176](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62176))

#### Bug fixes

- GitHub Copilot session costs use the amount Copilot charged instead of the catalog estimate, and content-filter errors name the filter that blocked the response. ([#62034](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62034))
- GitHub Copilot picks up a new API endpoint after a plan change on its next model refresh, so you no longer have to sign in again. ([#62171](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62171))
- Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer log you out when the TUI, desktop app, background service or several projects refresh the same login at once. ([#62827](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62827))
- A temporary failure while refreshing an MCP OAuth token keeps your login for the next try instead of marking the server `needs_auth`. ([#63012](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63012))
- MCP tool calls no longer fail when the server's result doesn't match the tool's own output schema, so completed actions aren't reported as failed. ([#61254](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61254))
- MCP prompts stay available when refreshing a server's prompt list fails. ([#62266](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62266))
- With `background_compaction` on, a background summary no longer stops a running Claude Agent session mid tool call. ([#63025](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63025))
- After `opencode auth logout` on a `.well-known` integration, its remote providers and policies stop applying until you log back in. ([#62760](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62760))
- OpenCode Console workspace policies still apply when Console's instructions or skills fail to load. ([#62702](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62702))
- Cloudflare AI Gateway providers set up with only `gatewayApiKey` now send that key. ([#62574](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62574))
- A v1 model override that sets only some capabilities no longer resets the others, so catalog capabilities like PDF input are kept. ([#62573](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62573))
- A v1 provider config that sets both `api` and `options.baseURL` keeps `options.baseURL`. ([#62570](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62570))
- Legacy model references with an inline variant, such as `"openai/gpt-5#high"`, keep the variant. ([#62254](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62254))
- A fresh install imports saved provider credentials from the legacy `auth.json`, and skips an invalid one with a warning instead of stopping setup. ([#62568](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62568))
- Cache warming stops for a session when a ping rebuilds the cache instead of reading it, counts its interval from when a request was sent, and no longer pings during compaction or after the session is deleted. ([#62926](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62926), [#62941](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62941), [#62972](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62972))
- Tokens and cost from `session.generate` requests, including cache warming pings, count toward the session's totals. ([#63006](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63006))
- Under zsh, a glob that matches nothing, like `rm *.tmp`, is passed through as bash does instead of stopping the command. ([#62141](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62141))
- Truncated shell output that starts mid-line drops the partial first line, so the "showing lines X–Y" notice is exact. ([#62141](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62141))
- On Windows, multi-line commands no longer lose everything after the first line with PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store. ([#62522](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62522))
- `read` no longer cuts an emoji in half when it shortens a long line. ([#62575](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62575))
- Generated session titles no longer include the model's commentary. Thanks [@shanebishop1](https://github.com/shanebishop1). ([#62267](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62267))
- Markdown agents whose `description` starts with a bracketed tag, like `[Beta] Reviews code`, now load. ([#62250](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62250))
- Markdown agent and command files that fail to load log a warning with the file path and frontmatter error. ([#62464](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62464), [#62251](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62251))
- Markdown agent discovery skips `node_modules`. ([#62571](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62571))
- Failed plugin installs from git show git's own error instead of "An unknown git error occurred". ([#62261](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62261))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- The update and confirm dialogs have buttons you can move between with `←`/`→` and `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`. ([#62906](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62906))
- The model picker no longer has a **Usage** action; use `/usage` instead. ([#62927](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62927))

#### Bug fixes

- Session exports are saved in the current working directory instead of the system temp folder. ([#62253](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62253))
- Typing a child session's exact ID in the open-session menu lists that session. ([#62262](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62262))
- The TUI follows the terminal's current light or dark mode instead of a cached palette. ([#62248](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62248))

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- Right-click a side panel tab to **Close tabs to the right**. `⌘W` closes side panel tabs wherever focus is, the new **Close session tab** command (`⌥⌘W` or `Ctrl+Alt+W`) always closes the session tab, and `⌘⇧T` reopens the last closed side panel or session tab where it was. ([#62922](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62922))
- Added **Mark as read** and **Mark as unread** to the menus for tabs, Home rows, project rows and inbox cards, and **Rename** to inbox cards. ([#62889](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62889))
- The answer you pick in the question dock shows as a raised card. ([#62896](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62896))
- Inline rename and custom-answer fields no longer show a focus border. ([#62919](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62919))

#### Bug fixes

- On Windows and Linux, `Ctrl+Shift+R` toggles the review panel again instead of reloading the window. ([#62567](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62567))
- Closing the last side panel tab slides the panel shut. ([#62758](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62758))
- Selects, menus, tooltips and toasts opened from a dialog are reachable by screen readers. ([#62913](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62913))
- An error appears when a path can't be opened in its default app. ([#62572](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62572))
- Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All in the right-click menu follow the app language. ([#62252](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62252))
- Ukrainian tool titles use nouns. ([#62263](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62263))
- Scrolling titlebar search results no longer jumps back when late results arrive, the inbox no longer announces already-running sessions as working on load, and the quote toolbar comes back after `Escape`. ([#62597](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62597))

### SDK

#### Improvements

- `session.generate` returns `tokens` and `cost` along with `text`. ([#62835](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62835))
- `credential.updated` includes the `integrationID` and `credentialID` of the login that changed. ([#62762](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62762))
- Predicate questions in `client.experimental.generate.decisions` accept optional `criteria: { true?, false? }`. ([#62819](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62819))

### Extensions

#### Improvements

- ACP clients can redirect a running turn with the `_session/steering` extension, advertised as `_meta.steering.supported` in `initialize`. Thanks [@smagnuso](https://github.com/smagnuso). ([#54394](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/54394))

name: v2.14.9 — Skills load for judgement calls too, even with many other skills installed.
body:
Skills load for judgement calls too, even with many other skills installed.

- **50 skills** (patch bump each): the "or asks" part of each description now covers the usual judgement calls in its area: choosing between two options ("which promise to lead with", "screen recording or AI avatar"), whether something is okay or fair ("is it fair to say a rival lacks offline mode", "is this markup allowed"), and whether it's enough ("are six directory listings enough"). Lower-value list items were cut to pay for it, so the pack stays at 18,662 characters and all 53 skills keep their descriptions with 90 other skills installed. On judgement-style prompts nobody read while writing the change, the right skill was picked for about 90% (92.5% twice, 89.6% for the shipped wording, from 66.5%) with 90 other skills installed and 95.3% (from 85.8%) with the pack alone, with no false triggers. programmatic-seo, revops, and signup are unchanged.
- **Trigger eval**: a fourth held-out set (`heldout4.json`, judgement-style), used unread to judge this change.

## Skill ZIP assets

Complete source catalog: 53 skills.
Claude web target: 53 skills with reviewed short descriptions.
Perplexity Computer target: 53 skills.

Choose `<name>-claude-web.zip` for the documented single-folder web upload format.
Choose `<name>-perplexity.zip` for Perplexity Computer (SKILL.md at the archive root).
Source ZIPs retain original metadata; they are not substitutes for omitted web ZIPs.
Live client upload, account limits, and invocation behavior have not been verified.

Web omissions (also recorded in `claude-web-manifest.json`):
- None.

name: v2.14.8 — Skills now load for advice and judgement questions, not just requests to make something.
body:
Skills now load for advice and judgement questions, not just requests to make something.

- **Every skill** (patch bump each): each description now names the questions the skill answers ("or asks whether a result is real, when to stop a test, or which version won") next to what it makes. Descriptions that only said "write", "plan", or "create" lost questions like "should we say they lack SSO?" or "where would you look for buyers?": the model answered from general knowledge instead of loading the skill. Total 18,676 characters (from 19,259), so all 53 skills keep their descriptions even with 90 other skills installed (2 dropped before). On a judgement-style test set nobody read while writing the change, the right skill was picked for 87.7% of prompts (from 73.6%) with the pack alone and 73.6% (from about 60%) with 90 other skills installed. Advice-style prompts with other skills installed went from about 84% to 94%, and the original set reaches 100% alone.
- **Trigger eval**: two more held-out sets (`heldout2.json` advice-style, `heldout3.json` judgement-style), seven `heldout.json` prompts now include the material they mention, and missed rows record the model's reply. The README covers run-to-run noise (about plus or minus 4 points on crowded runs) and when to use `--repeat`.

## Skill ZIP assets

Complete source catalog: 53 skills.

name: v2.14.3 — Shorter skill descriptions, so Claude Code shows all of them.
body:
Shorter skill descriptions, so Claude Code shows all of them.

- **Every skill** (patch bump each): descriptions rewritten to 491 characters or fewer, 19,259 in total (down from 42,105). Claude Code caps the skill listing it sends the model at about 30,000 characters, and past the cap a skill appears as a bare name: before this release, 26 of 53 skills had no description in the listing even with the pack installed alone; now none do. Each description says what the skill does, the distinct situations it covers, its operative rule, and the neighbouring skill to use instead, starting with "When the user wants to". On the new trigger eval (Sonnet), the right skill was picked for 98.7% of prompts (from 96.2%) with the pack alone, 96.9% (from 94.3%) with 90 other skills installed, and 89.6% (from 81.1%) on held-out prompts written without reading the descriptions, with other skills installed.
- **Trigger eval** (`scripts/trigger-eval.mjs`, `evals/triggers/`): runs prompts through headless Claude Code with the pack as a plugin and scores the first skill invoked. Includes 171 prompts across all skills, a 114-prompt held-out set, an option to install other skills alongside, and contract tests.
- **Description budget**: `scripts/check-versions.mjs` now fails a PR if a description passes 500 characters or the pack passes 24,000. AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain the limit and how to test description changes.

name: Humanizer v4.0.0
body:
Humanizer 4.0.0 lets the skill add a specific detail where the text is generic, and it rewrites the skill's own instructions and examples to be clearer.

A rewrite may now contain a detail that was not in your text. If you rely on the old rule, stay on v3.1.0.

## What changed

- The skill no longer forbids adding facts. Where the text is generic, it now adds a specific detail it knows to be true. It still keeps every claim the original made and treats a lost or changed claim as an error. This reverses the no-invention rule from 2.9.0. Patterns 14 and 17 follow the same change.
- Reworked 15 "After" examples in `SKILL.md` and both README examples. Several were vaguer or stiffer than the text they replaced, used phrases from the skill's own watch lists, or changed a stated fact.
- File mode now reads the whole current file before editing, even one written in the same session. Its summary says how many sections it reviewed, so a partial pass is visible (#326, #327).
- Text being edited can contain fake closing tags or notes from an "operator" or a "system message". The skill now treats those as material to edit, never as instructions (#317).
- Rewrote unclear sentences in `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. Coined terms such as "riders" and "shape edits" became plain words, and sentences that only announced or repeated a neighbor are gone. Step 3 now checks for dropped or changed facts first. Pattern 15 is now "Shallow -ing phrases". The README gives `/humanizer` as the only command (#330).
- Added a blank line above each pattern label in `SKILL.md` so GitHub shows every label and example on its own line (#329).
- The skill description no longer cites Wikipedia. The credit stays in the Source section and the README (#321).
- Added a pi package manifest, so `pi install git:github.com/blader/humanizer` installs the skill (#315).
- Removed the `$schema` key from the Claude plugin manifest, which caused a sync warning (#307).

Thanks to @marlandoj, @mathewgeejo, @AYastrebov, @thanhnguyentung95, @devilliersdutoit, and @Josephqaz for the fixes and reports in this release.

name: v0.42.0
body:
### New Features

- Added **saved flows** (experimental): record a browser task once, then replay its requests. A run tries direct HTTP first, then the same request from the page, then a replay of the recorded commands, and saves the tier that worked. Runs send requests only to public addresses, and saving waits for in-flight requests and follows redirects to the end (#2236, #2397, #2432, #2433, #2444)
- **MCP tools** now list only the shared arguments each tool uses (#2311)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **session reuse and relaunch**, now decided in one place in the daemon. A connection target is kept only after an attach succeeds, and security settings persist across daemon restarts (#2396, #2418, #2429)
- Fixed **Safari and iOS WebDriver sessions** being dropped (#2385)
- Fixed **fill and type** altering literal text, and **mouse and element coordinates** losing fractional values (#2394, #2393)

name: v15.15.1
body:
## No replay after an outage

When the worker was down or refused a capture, some capture paths kept that work and sent it again later, which could start model calls nobody asked for. They now drop what the worker refused and carry on with new work (#5663):

- **Transcript capture:** a transcript line the worker refuses or cannot take is skipped. Before, the watcher stopped at that line and, once the worker was back, sent it again with every line after it. A restart no longer resends lines from an outage either.
- **Cowork:** a prompt, observation or summary that fails to send is dropped instead of being spooled and sent again by a later hook. Only session start, session end and subagent stop events are still spooled, and prompts, observations and summaries left in an older spool are removed on its next flush.
- **OpenCode:** a session start the worker refused is sent once, like observations and summaries, instead of being retried in the background for about 10 seconds.

## Fixes

- **Redaction:** Grafana service account tokens (`glsa_`), Grafana Cloud tokens (`glc_`) and Postman API keys (`PMAK-`) are redacted, by the worker and by the Cowork shim. Turn either off by name with `CLAUDE_MEM_REDACT_DISABLED_BUILTINS` (`grafana_token`, `postman_key`) (#5662, thanks @kevin9327).
- **OpenClaw:** `<private>` content is removed from tool output before the output is cut to 1,000 characters. Before, a cut inside a private block dropped its closing tag, so the private text was stored. Text after an unclosed `<private>` tag is now dropped too (#5663).
- **Status and doctor:** `claude-mem status` names every dependency in words, such as "Observer data directory setup required" instead of `observer_dir: setup_required`, and its hint points to `claude-mem doctor` instead of a Settings screen that does not show these. `doctor` shows a status from a newer worker instead of dropping it (#5661).
- **Work state:** `Done` and `Dropped` close an item in any letter case, everywhere. Before, saving an owner-goals item as `Done` was refused although every reader already treated it as closed (#5661).
- **CCS Align:** a corrupt exclusion file is refused instead of being read as empty, so excluded observations stay excluded and the file is not overwritten (#5663).
- **Viewer:** observations of type `sensitive` get their own "Sensitive" filter on the session page instead of being counted under "Other" (#5663).

## Also in this release

- **Setup and My Work:** each setup, billing, scan and refresh state is defined once and shared by the installer, the worker and the pages, so a new state fails the typecheck until every screen handles it (#5661).
- **Tests:** about 60,000 lines of tests removed: tests that only checked their own fixtures, duplicate cases (folded into tables) and four duplicate copies of the agent-cost-report Python tests. Kept regression tests run production code (#5663).
- **CI:** Bun is pinned to 1.4.4, ripgrep is installed, the Cowork runner and agent-cost-report Python tests run, and tool-heavy suites moved to the integration lane (#5663).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.15.0...v15.15.1

name: v15.15.0
body:
## Critical fix

- **The worker no longer freezes on its first image (#5601):** a worker started from a plugin root with no `node_modules` (the Claude Code marketplace clone) could freeze for good. Bun's auto-install loaded sharp's wasm build, whose first call blocks Bun's main thread, so timers and `/api/health` stopped and hooks kept reclaiming the worker. Now every worker, server and plugin spawn runs `bun --no-install`, the installer starts the worker from the plugin cache copy where it just ran `bun install`, and the media converter refuses sharp's wasm build before decoding, so a worker started some other way reports `decoder_unavailable` instead of freezing (#5653). Thanks to @vieGPT for the report and to @Kirat0201 for reproducing it and proposing the approach.

## New

- **One Rules + Tools line at session start:** the SessionStart header (project and time, Mode, Legend, Format, Fetch, Stats) is now one line, `Access Claude-Mem Rules + Tools: ~/.claude-mem/RULES-AND-TOOLS.md`. That file holds the format, legend, mode, how to fetch details, the work-state rule and memory-use guidance, and is rewritten only when its text changes. The terminal banner now ends on a closing line with the viewer link and how many timeline lines are shown (#5654).
- **Savings settings removed:** the context header no longer prints a savings line, so `CLAUDE_MEM_CONTEXT_SHOW_SAVINGS_AMOUNT` and `CLAUDE_MEM_CONTEXT_SHOW_SAVINGS_PERCENT` and their viewer toggle are gone. Settings files that still carry them load as before (#5654).

## Fixes

- **Installer:** the setup state is prepared before the browser opens, so a quick first choice is no longer erased and the installer no longer waits for a choice you already made (#5631, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Context:** the prior-session reply shown at startup is read from the end of the transcript instead of loading the whole file, so long sessions start faster and very large transcripts keep that context (#5625, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Terminal banner:** when the banner cut lands exactly on a line boundary, the whole line that fits is kept, and the line count also counts rows in the plain block format (#5654).
- **Tests:** the server's semantic context route probes the embedding model only where pgvector exists, so CI no longer times out on a cold model download (#5659).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.14.0...v15.15.0

name: v15.14.0
body:
## New

- **Focus areas in My Work:** My Work now opens on an overview of your focus areas. Each area gets a card with bundled concept artwork, its goal and live request counts; open one to see its requests. The setup reveal screen uses the same view. Artwork can be set to full, compact or off, and the images ship with the plugin, so nothing is generated or fetched at runtime (#5652).
- **claude-mem can update itself:** the worker checks once a day for the release promoted in `releases/promoted-release.json`, and installs only a newer version that npm shows as published by the release workflow with provenance, only while you have been away for a while. A failed update puts the previous version back. `npx claude-mem doctor` shows an Auto-update row. Turn it off with `CLAUDE_MEM_AUTO_UPDATE=false`; Claude Code's own update switches (`DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` and friends) also turn it off. New installs register the marketplace with Claude Code's background update off, so only one updater runs. See the new auto-update docs page (#5500).
- **Startup context is the timeline alone:** the SessionStart message is now the header lines followed by the timeline, ending on the newest entry. The longer work-state and memory-use instructions moved to the claude-mem MCP server's instructions. The terminal banner has the same shape (#5487).
- **Faster hooks:** hooks run from a small hook-only bundle instead of the full worker bundle. One hook takes about half the time and memory; a dozen parallel hooks use about a quarter of the CPU (#5541, thanks @bulanovk).
- **Raw tool evidence search (opt-in, local):** with `CLAUDE_MEM_TOOL_USES_SEARCH_ENABLED=true`, a local `search` with `deep: true` looks through stored tool input and output when the observation search finds nothing, and returns `#T` IDs for `get_tool_uses` (#5167, thanks @ShitK).
- **Korean UI:** the viewer, My Work, setup and Observation TV can be shown in Korean (#5522, thanks @BaeJinSeop).

## Privacy and security

- **Context:** privacy filters now also apply to prior-session replies shown at startup (#5626).
- **Backups:** SQLite snapshots are created readable only by you (#5642).
- **Media:** cloud uploads stop starting after you opt out (#5622).
- **Redaction:** cookie header values are redacted, matching the Cowork shim (#5591, thanks @DeryFerd), and the Cowork shim now redacts the key shapes it still sent verbatim (#5543, thanks @DeryFerd).
- **Worker:** read routes that resolve a project from `cwd` are guarded (#5590, thanks @DeryFerd).
- **Auth:** stored access tokens that are not strings are rejected (#5506, thanks @Kirat0201).
- **Launcher:** macOS signing is verified before the launcher is put in place (#5503, thanks @Kirat0201).
- **Telemetry:** a saved consent choice is kept when identifiers are created (#5629).

## Installers and integrations

- **Atomic config writes:** Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Kimi, Antigravity, Hermes, Grok Bot and OMP config and hook files are written atomically, so an interrupted install can't leave a broken file (#5592, #5593, #5594, #5595, #5596, #5597, #5598, #5599, thanks @DeryFerd).
- **Cursor:** `uninstall` removes the hooks and MCP server that `install --ide cursor` adds (#5584, thanks @tanishqbaweja).
- **Installer:** tool version probes, browser-setup worker requests and npm child processes are bounded, and npm descendants are terminated on timeout (#5634, #5638, #5644).
- **Installer:** existing host installs are found in their configured folders, non-executable paths are skipped during runtime discovery, Roo Code is detected by its marketplace ID, and a compatible tree-sitter on PATH is used during repair (#5552, #5556, #5560, #5576, thanks @Kirat0201).
- **Hooks:** hooks dispatch through the installed plugin resolver (#5504, thanks @Kirat0201).
- **OpenCode:** one bounded live observer handoff (#5621). **Pi:** tool results are normalized for evidence (#5605). **Goose:** executable paths are quoted in the YAML config (#5606). **Devin:** only its own tool-map entries are translated (#5512, thanks @Kirat0201). **Telegram:** sends are bounded (#5636).
- **Adapters:** explicit tool failures are kept as evidence (#5620).
- **DSH:** worker MCP error results are passed through and failures during response body reads are classified correctly (#5604, #5619).

## My Work

- Lists are ordered by original activity time, owner goals replay in event order, and conversation titles are scoped to their platform (#5580, #5589, #5561).
- Stale group evidence is removed when conversations move, invalid observation file entries are skipped, Git branch products are attributed to confirmed remote updates, and deleted Windows temp folders are recognized (#5587, #5585, #5533, #5554).
- Large histories and catalogs stay under SQLite's limits, deeply nested publishing results are handled, ledger snapshots use isolated atomic writes, and deliverable revisions that share a short hash are kept (#5588, #5549, #5579, #5582, #5536).
- The empty Rules page explains that it is waiting for an agent, the first live request is announced after an empty list, and setup memory search cards show the recorded agent (#5575, thanks @Kirat0201; #5564, #5574).

## Search, context and memory

- Smart search bounds source memory and accepts portable path filters; file-history ranking and index pages are faster (#5534, #5586, #5602).
- Search keeps multiline titles in one table row, keeps zero-valued date bounds, propagates SQLite failures before replacing corpora, and keeps distinct DSH results (#5583, #5520, thanks @Kirat0201; #5610, #5548).
- Context selects equal-time rows consistently, enforces mode filters on the server, respects a literal `~` and `+`-prefixed filenames in shell reads (#5608, #5623, #5633, #5510, thanks @Kirat0201).
- Knowledge corpora keep source evidence and identities, overlapping operations can't overwrite saved state, and cancelled queries are not saved (#5528, #5612, #5648).
- Smart navigation shows Rust traits, implementations and data definitions (#5531).
- Dedup reads are bounded and the IDF model is rebuilt from a locked snapshot (#5632, #5613).
- CLAUDE.md honors a zero observation count and `claude-md clean` keeps authored indentation (#5508, thanks @Kirat0201; #5566).

## Backup, restore, import and sync

- Restore refuses newer-schema snapshots and remote-worker restores before touching live data, reports committed swaps despite cleanup errors, keeps damaged recovery pairs, and protects the selected restore point from retention (#5649, #5562, #5624, #5630, #5532).
- Backups account for WAL pages on the snapshot volume (#5627).
- Import keeps observation provenance and reinforcement history, accepts a UTF-8 BOM, indexes legacy lists consistently and exits nonzero when rows are rejected (#5609, #5518, #5514, #5516, thanks @Kirat0201).
- Sync removes replica vectors after remote tombstones, refreshes vector metadata after project remaps, quarantines out-of-range numbers, rejects malformed ports and protects excluded folders in stale marketplace directories (#5647, #5645, #5611, #5573, #5525).
- Chroma persists checkpoints for prototype-named projects (#5607). Notion exports stay within UTF-8 request limits (#5529). Memory export keeps its deadline through the response body (#5547).

## Server and CLI

- Server: generation completions are metered once, reasoning corrections stay within the job's paid-send cap, operator generation state changes are locked, legacy ingestion routes get usage guards, event polling stops on disconnect, shutdown cleanup finishes after errors, and queue health reads are bounded during Redis outages (#5640, #5615, #5650, #5641, #5651, #5628, #5617).
- PostgreSQL: explicit TLS policy is kept, failed pool connections recover, idempotent writes skip inference, redelivered events are linked, and scoped job counts are not compared to global totals (#5637, #5537, #5538, #5546, #5559).
- CLI: completed generation jobs are not retried, key rotation stops when the previous key lookup fails, command-owned job pools close, signal-terminated children report failure, and search can query a worker without a local plugin (#5603, #5618, #5639, #5569, #5568).
- MCP: the npm MCP server launches in the invoking checkout, an empty explicit port is rejected, server MCP clients don't see unavailable local operations, and setup prints the server MCP endpoint (#5553, #5571, #5551, #5563).
- SQLite handles are closed when initialization fails; rejected worker run promises are observed; transient media cloud reads stay retryable (#5635, #5616, #5614).
- Smaller fixes: legacy SQLite timestamps show the right year, Unicode survives prompt-history shortening, single-quoted skip reasons are accepted, the Pro trial pitch is skipped for accounts already on trial or Pro, log tails stream correctly, and folder context generation reports incomplete work (#5557, #5550, #5558, #5545, #5526, #5565, #5572).

## Docs

- Translated READMEs have fixed links and headings (#5527, thanks @vietmy1711), and two old release notes now describe cloud sync and telemetry correctly (#5577, thanks @Kirat0201).

Thanks to @Afloat16 for the large majority of the fixes in this release.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.13.0...v15.14.0

name: supervision-0.31.6
body:
# v0.31.6: Key points on empty frames, zero-shot Transformers results, and drawing on grayscale and palette scenes

A fixes-only patch: fewer crashes on empty frames, more Transformers models that load, and annotators that draw on any scene.

- **KeyPoints** filters stop raising `TypeError` on video frames with no people.
- Grounding DINO and RF-DETR segmentation results load, and OWLv2 detections get real class names.
- `DetectionsSmoother` keeps unconfirmed tracks as separate boxes instead of one averaged box.
- Labels and images draw on grayscale, BGRA and Pillow palette scenes.
- Integer boxes no longer wrap around, and narrow-integer mask shifts no longer crash.

It's a drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you use ViTPose class IDs, YOLO-NAS confidences or compare stored outputs.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Key points survive empty frames

`sv.KeyPoints.empty()` now holds empty `class_id`, `keypoint_confidence` and `detection_confidence` arrays instead of `None`, and selecting key points from it returns an empty result. Pose connectors such as `sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics` return it for every frame without people, so the documented filters raised `TypeError` mid-video. ViTPose poses from `sv.KeyPoints.from_transformers` now all get class ID `0` instead of `0..N-1`, and `sv.KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas` keeps each pose score as `detection_confidence`, so `with_nms` works on YOLO-NAS poses. (#2911, #2920, #2914, #2909)

```python
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints.empty()  # what pose connectors return for an empty frame
len(key_points[key_points.detection_confidence > 0.5])
# 0.31.6: 0  -> correct, an empty frame has nothing to filter
# 0.31.5: TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'
#         -> bug, the confidence arrays were None
key_points[:, [0, 1]].xy.shape
# 0.31.6: (0, 0, 2)  -> correct, no poses so nothing to select
# 0.31.5: IndexError  -> bug, selection crashed on an empty frame
```

### Zero-shot and RF-DETR results from Transformers

`sv.Detections.from_transformers` now reads results of `post_process_grounded_object_detection`. Grounding DINO results used to raise `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'cpu'`; they now load with the matched phrases as class names and `class_id=None`. OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo keep the text query index as `class_id` and take class names from `text_labels`; `id2label=model.config.id2label` used to name them `LABEL_0`, `LABEL_1`. RF-DETR instance segmentation results requested with `return_binary_maps=True` load too. If a result has no recognized fields, the error now points to the official `rfdetr` package, whose `predict()` returns `sv.Detections` directly. (#2913, #2912, #2921)

```python
import supervision as sv

# results = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(...)[0]  # Grounding DINO
detections = sv.Detections.from_transformers(results)
detections.data["class_name"]  # matched phrases, e.g. ["a cat", "a dog"]
detections.class_id  # None
```

### `DetectionsSmoother` keeps unconfirmed tracks apart

Detections with a negative `tracker_id`, which some trackers use for tracks they haven't confirmed yet, now pass through `sv.DetectionsSmoother` unchanged. They used to share one history and come back as a single averaged box. Frames where only some tracks keep oriented-box corners no longer raise a merge error. (#2926, #2923)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

smoother = sv.DetectionsSmoother()
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10], [100, 0, 110, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([-1, -1]),  # not confirmed by the tracker yet
)
smoother.update_with_detections(detections).xyxy.tolist()
# 0.31.6: [[0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0], [100.0, 0.0, 110.0, 10.0]]
#         -> correct, two objects stay two boxes
# 0.31.5: [[50.0, 0.0, 60.0, 10.0]]
#         -> bug, both were averaged into one phantom box
```

### Drawing on grayscale, BGRA and palette scenes

`sv.RichLabelAnnotator` annotates grayscale scenes, shaped `(H, W)` or `(H, W, 1)` or given as a Pillow grayscale image, and `sv.draw_image` draws on grayscale and BGRA scenes. Boxes and labels on Pillow palette images now come out in the colors you asked for, not black. Labels such as `0` or `False` show up as text instead of empty boxes. (#2916, #2906, #2907, #2892)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)  # grayscale frame
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[10.0, 10.0, 60.0, 60.0]]), class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.RichLabelAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections, labels=["car"]).shape
# 0.31.6: (100, 100)  -> correct, grayscale scene annotated in place
# 0.31.5: TypeError: color must be int or single-element tuple
#         -> bug, grayscale scenes were not supported
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

Nothing was removed, renamed or deprecated, but a few fixes change what existing code returns:

- **Different values:** ViTPose poses from `KeyPoints.from_transformers` all get `class_id` `0`; use `np.arange(len(key_points))` if you used it as a per-person index. (#2914) `KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas(...).as_detections().confidence` reports the model score instead of the mean key point confidence. (#2909) OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo class names come from `text_labels`, even when you pass `id2label`. (#2913) `xywh_to_xyxy` returns `int64` for integer input, or `float64` when a corner exceeds the `int64` range. (#2922)
- **Different rows and shapes:** `DetectionsSmoother` returns unconfirmed detections as their own rows, after the smoothed tracks. (#2926) `KeyPoints.empty()` fields are empty arrays, not `None`. (#2911) With OpenCV, `resize_image`, `scale_image` and `letterbox_image` keep `(H, W, 1)` input as `(H, W, 1)`. (#2905)
- **Different counts, colors and labels:** `PolygonZone` no longer counts anchors in `(-1, 0)`. (#2924) `ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` rounds colors like `to_hex`, so some move by one level. (#2903) Labels such as `0` or `False`, drawn as empty boxes before, now show their text. (#2892)
- **Without OpenCV:** `mask_to_polygons` returns polygons in OpenCV's `RETR_TREE` order (#2900), image writes save most non-`uint8` images instead of failing, though multi-channel non-`uint8` TIFFs still fail (#2901), and `HeatMapAnnotator` colors move closer to OpenCV (#2904). Regenerate stored references made with the NumPy fallback.
- **New error:** drawing on a Pillow palette image whose palette is full and has no opaque entry raises `ValueError` instead of drawing wrong colors. (#2907)

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🌱 Changed

- `Detections.from_transformers` suggests the official `rfdetr` package when a result has no recognized fields, and its docs recommend `rfdetr` for RF-DETR models. (#2921)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Key points**

- `KeyPoints.empty()` holds empty `class_id`, `keypoint_confidence` and `detection_confidence` arrays instead of `None`, so confidence filters no longer raise `TypeError` on frames without poses. (#2911)
- Selecting key points from an empty result, as in `key_points[:, [0, 1]]`, returns an empty result instead of raising `IndexError`. (#2920)
- `KeyPoints.from_transformers` gives every ViTPose pose class ID `0`; with the old `0..N-1` IDs, keypoint mAP against person targets scored too low and per-class `EdgeAnnotator` edges raised `ValueError`. (#2914)
- `KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas` keeps each pose score as `detection_confidence`, so `with_nms` no longer raises `ValueError` on YOLO-NAS poses. (#2909)

**Model connectors**

- `Detections.from_transformers` reads zero-shot results from `post_process_grounded_object_detection`: Grounding DINO no longer raises `AttributeError`, and OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo take class names from `text_labels`. (#2913)
- `Detections.from_transformers` reads RF-DETR instance segmentation results with `return_binary_maps=True`, pairing binary maps with `segments_info` by position; an empty `(0, H, W)` stack gives empty masks. (#2912)
- `Classifications.from_clip` and `Classifications.from_timm` accept bfloat16 outputs, including mixed-precision inference, and return float32 probabilities for them. (#2894)

**Tracking, zones and box math**

- `DetectionsSmoother` returns detections with a negative `tracker_id` unchanged instead of averaging them into one box; when those rows carry oriented corners, confirmed tracks without corner history get their smoothed axis-aligned bounds as corners. (#2926)
- `DetectionsSmoother` returns all tracked boxes when only some smoothed tracks keep oriented corners, using smoothed axis-aligned bounds instead of raising a merge error. (#2923)
- `PolygonZone` excludes negative subpixel anchors before rounding, so an anchor just outside the top or left edge is no longer counted as pixel zero. (#2924)
- `xywh_to_xyxy` promotes integer coordinates before adding widths and heights: a `uint8` box `[200, 20, 100, 40]` becomes `[200, 20, 300, 60]` instead of wrapping its right edge to `44`. (#2922)
- `move_masks` computes slice bounds without integer overflow, so narrow integer offsets work on larger frames and no-overlap shifts with narrow or unsigned integer offsets return empty masks instead of raising. (#2918)
- `JSONSink` keeps an exception raised inside a `with` block when writing or closing the file also fails; the cleanup error is logged. (#2902)

**Annotators and colors**

- `RichLabelAnnotator` annotates grayscale scenes, `(H, W)`, `(H, W, 1)` or Pillow grayscale modes, instead of raising `TypeError` or `ValueError`. (#2916)
- Annotators draw the requested colors on Pillow palette images (`P`, `PA`) instead of other colors or black. (#2907)
- `draw_image` draws on grayscale and BGRA scenes instead of raising a NumPy broadcast error. (#2906)
- `LabelAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` draw labels such as `0`, `np.int64(0)`, `0.0` and `False` as text instead of empty background boxes. (#2892)
- `ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` rounds colors to 8-bit values as Matplotlib's `to_hex` does instead of truncating them. (#2903)

**Images and the NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `resize_image`, `scale_image` and `letterbox_image` return `(H, W, 1)` for `(H, W, 1)` input on OpenCV installs too, and `tint_image` and `grayscale_image` accept `(H, W, 1)` images. (#2905)
- Image writes without OpenCV, such as `ImageSink.save_image` and dataset exports, keep 16-bit PNGs and save a saturated 8-bit copy for JPEG, BMP and WebP, instead of raising `TypeError` or returning `False`. (#2901)
- `mask_to_polygons` lists polygons in OpenCV's `RETR_TREE` order without OpenCV too, and one- and two-pixel contours are `int32`. (#2900)
- `HeatMapAnnotator` colors without OpenCV follow OpenCV's float32 HSV-to-BGR arithmetic instead of coming out one level off. (#2904)
- `create_batches` yields each full batch before consuming the next item, so stopping early leaves the rest of the source intact. (#2893)

### 📚 Docs

- New how-to section on attaching tracker IDs back to key points in [Track Objects](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/how_to/track_objects/). (#2896)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors Mohammad Sohail Shaikh, Vlad Voropaev, Ahmet Mert Özacar and peterolkhov!

- **Oke Iyanuoluwa Enoch** (@Iyanuoluwa007, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iyanuoluwa-enoch-oke/)) – drawing on grayscale, BGRA and Pillow palette scenes, selecting key points from empty results, and OpenCV-matching contours, image writes and HSV conversion in the NumPy fallback.
- **Mohammad Sohail Shaikh** (@sohailshk, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohdsohailshk/)) – kept YOLO-NAS pose scores, gave `KeyPoints.empty()` empty arrays, and kept unconfirmed tracks out of `DetectionsSmoother` averaging.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-v-engineer)) – loaded zero-shot and RF-DETR segmentation results in `from_transformers` and fixed ViTPose class IDs.
- **Vlad Voropaev** (@voropaevv, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thevladvoropaev/)) – fixed `DetectionsSmoother` on mixed oriented-box tracks and `PolygonZone` edge anchors.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammadhijjawi)) – drew falsy labels as text and rounded Matplotlib palette colors like `to_hex`.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) – accepted bfloat16 classification outputs and fixed overflow in `move_masks`.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/vaishnavi-d-9a42a9374)) – kept `with` block errors in `JSONSink` and made `create_batches` stop consuming early.
- **peterolkhov** (@peterolkhov) – fixed integer overflow in `xywh_to_xyxy`.
- **Kari Pikkarainen** (@kari-pikkarainen, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karipikkarainen/)) – wrote the how-to on attaching tracker IDs to key points and corrected the contributing guide.
- **Ahmet Mert Özacar** (@AhmetMert01) – type-checked the docstring example tests.
- **Jirka Borovec** (@Borda, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/jirka-borovec)) – pointed `from_transformers` users to `rfdetr` and prepared the release.

*Automated contributions: dependabot, pre-commit.ci*

______________________________________________________________________

**Full changelog**: <https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/compare/0.31.5...0.31.6>
*Co-authored with [`/oss:release`](https://borda.github.io/AI-Rig/cc_oss/#ossrelease).*

name: MinerU 4.2.0
body:
## 4.2.0

MinerU 4.2.0 重点升级 WebUI 交互与结果溯源，改善复杂 PDF、公式和表格的解析质量，并完善设备选择、模型缓存、服务管理与输入安全。以下为相对 4.1.0 的累计更新，包含 4.1.x 期间已发布的改进。

### WebUI 交互与结果溯源

- **新增原文与结果双向定位**：点击 PDF 或图片中的区域，即可定位并高亮对应的解析内容；点击结果中的段落、标题、公式或图表，也可返回原文位置。跨页合并内容支持切换来源页。
- **增强布局可视化**：合并后的段落、列表和表格可关联多个原文区域，并通过连线展示合并关系，方便检查阅读顺序、内容归属和跨页合并结果。
- **新增结果目录导航**：根据标题生成可折叠目录，支持快速跳转到对应内容。
- **重新设计上传区域**：集中呈现文件选择、拖放、粘贴、文件类型、上传进度和取消操作，让上传过程更清晰。
- **重做档位与页范围控件**：采用更紧凑的布局，优化选择与拖动体验，并展示解析服务的 CPU/GPU 运行状态。
- **加快 PDF 预览**：选择本地 PDF 后，浏览器直接预览完整文档，并行完成上传，减少预览等待和重复传输。
- **保持解析前后的预览状态**：解析完成后复用已加载的查看器，保留缩放状态，并以叠加标框展示布局结果。
- **减少重复处理**：复用已准备的输入文件、语义结果和素材，减少原文 PDF、布局 PDF 及预览文件的重复生成，加快结果预览与导出。

### PDF、公式与表格解析

- **改进行内公式识别**：Standard/Advanced 在 PDF 原生文本路径中，使用 VLM 识别表外行内公式区域；识别结果为空或无效时，保留局部公式识别模型回退。
- **保护脚注公式并改进页边区域处理**：修复脚注公式被错误改标或过滤的问题，减少公式、编号与正文之间的归属错误。
- **改进嵌套与重叠区域处理**：优化重复区域筛选与合并范围，减少重复文本和过度合并；修正图内标注的归属，并改善合并图片的阅读顺序。
- **统一布局检测行为**：恢复 ONNX 与 Torch 后端的逐类输出阈值，提高不同后端处理结果的一致性。
- **改善原生文本恢复**：完善空 ToUnicode 映射下的字符恢复，并在后置 OCR 和失败恢复后清理残留的 Unicode 私用区字符，减少缺字和乱码。
- **保留仿斜体正文**：修复整行字符经过倾斜变换时，正常正文被误判并丢失的问题。
- **修复旋转页面中的表格方向判断**：结合页面旋转信息解释原生文字方向，减少表格被错误旋转的问题。
- **保持表格内图片与公式完整**：避免表格恢复过程中将图片、公式拆散，或错误分配到多个单元格。
- **改善跨页表格输出**：保留单元格拼接处的文本边界，完善空白续接、稀疏空白行和共享跨行单元格的处理。

### 原生文档解析

- **利用 Tagged PDF 结构语义**：Flash 原生 PDF 文本解析可利用 Tagged PDF/PDF/UA 文档中的结构信息与阅读顺序；未覆盖或不可信的内容继续由几何规则处理。
- **改进段落续接**：结合缩进、句末位置等页面证据，改善大写字母开头的续接判断，以及跨页、跨栏段落合并。
- **改进原生表格恢复**：修复异常字形边界导致的行划分错误，以及部分数字表格中跨行单元格的归属问题。
- **改善字体粗细判断**：增强嵌入字体的字重解析，减少正常正文被误判为粗体的情况。
- **改善 Office 图片异常处理**：对部分超出图片处理资源限制的内容使用占位表示，避免单张图片导致整份文档解析失败。

### 设备选择、档位推荐与硬件诊断

- **统一进程内的设备选择**：模型加载、自动档位推荐和 llama.cpp 自动模式共享已确定的运行设备，减少重复探测与不同入口之间的行为差异。
- **改善多显卡识别**：通过物理 PCI 地址关联 Windows GPU 与显存信息，提高多显卡及同型号设备的匹配准确性。
- **调整自动档位推荐**：根据小模型后端实际选择的设备推荐档位。GPU 可开放全部档位；CPU 可用逻辑核数达到 4 核时开放 Basic，达到 12 核时开放 Standard。
- **完善 ONNX 独显自动选型**：Windows/Linux 自动模式增加独显总显存检查。总显存按 GiB 换算并四舍五入后达到 6 及以上，才直接选择 GPU；容量不足或无法确认时使用 CPU。
- **增加设备状态查询**：解析服务健康接口可返回已初始化的 CPU/GPU 运行状态，查询本身不触发设备选择。
- **加快硬件诊断**：并行执行隔离的运行时探测，按节输出报告；统一容量显示与设备摘要，并在 JSON 中保留完整诊断信息及候选设备的选择原因。
- **加快 CLI 帮助与版本查询**：按需加载命令入口，避免仅查看帮助或版本时初始化运行环境、读取用户配置。
- **改善运行时退出**：完善 VLM 关闭与资源释放，减少进程退出阶段的清理失败。

### Router 与 API

- **新增动态上游节点管理**：支持在运行期间查询、注册和移除远程解析节点，无需重启 Router。
- **支持节点平滑移除**：先停止向节点分配新任务，待已有任务、传输和结果引用释放后，再完成移除。
- **支持 Router 级联**：复用现有 V1 协议与结果租约，支持将下层 Router 作为上游节点接入，便于组织多层服务入口。
- **提供独立管理认证**：动态节点管理使用独立的管理凭证，与解析请求认证分离。
- **修复路径识别并统一文件名校验**：修复 CLI 相对路径和隐藏文件路径的格式识别；统一 Tasks、Router 与同步上传入口的文件名校验，拒绝路径型名称和控制字符。

### 模型下载与缓存校验

- **引入模型文件清单**：为整仓、目录和单文件资源记录预期文件及大小，在缓存复用时检查文件缺失、截断、失效链接和清单异常。
- **支持离线校验**：正常缓存可在不联网的情况下完成校验与复用，无需读取大体积权重文件计算哈希。
- **改善增量修复**：识别缺失或大小不符的文件，在重新下载时修复，并继续复用有效文件。
- **兼容旧完成标记**：旧缓存通过必要文件与分片检查后，可继续离线使用；具备网络条件时，后台核对对应版本的远端元数据并升级文件清单，不更新模型权重。

### 本机认证与输入安全

- **Doclib 增加持久化 Bearer Token 认证**：SDK 默认发现本机服务时自动读取凭证；直接调用 HTTP 接口时，需要携带有效 Token。
- **加强本机凭证保护**：按平台设置并校验 POSIX 私有权限及 macOS、Windows ACL，限制其他账户访问或替换凭证文件。
- **加强 URL 输入的 SSRF 防护**：连接前校验域名解析得到的全部地址，并固定连接已校验的公网 IP，拒绝内网、回环、链路本地、云元数据及其他特殊地址。
- **收紧 URL 输入下载行为**：采用直连方式，不跟随重定向，不使用环境中的 HTTP/HTTPS/ALL 代理设置。
- **执行文档资源限制**：当文档解压或结构展开超出预算时终止处理，覆盖 OOXML 解压、XLSX 合并区域展开等场景；通过 `resource_limit` 返回明确错误，并保留 Tasks 的逐文件失败信息。

### 升级提示

- **直接调用 Doclib HTTP 接口的客户端需要适配 Bearer Token 认证。** SDK 默认发现本机服务时自动读取凭证；显式指定服务地址或 Socket 路径时，需要同时提供 Token。
- **依赖内网 URL、重定向或环境代理下载输入文件的部署需要调整输入方式。** 内网文档可改为通过客户端上传。
- **设备配置变更需要重启相关进程后生效。** 运行设备确定后，在当前进程内保持稳定；ONNX 新增的独显显存门槛仅作用于自动模式。
- 最低依赖版本更新为 **DocVortex 0.6.21** 和 **ModelScope 1.39.1**。

---

## 4.2.0

MinerU 4.2.0 upgrades WebUI interaction and source tracing, improves parsing of complex PDFs, formulas, and tables, and strengthens device selection, model caching, service management, and input security. These are cumulative changes since 4.1.0, including improvements released in 4.1.x.

### WebUI interaction and source tracing

- **Bidirectional source navigation:** Click a region in a PDF or image to locate and highlight its parsed content, or click a parsed paragraph, heading, formula, or figure to return to its source. Content merged across pages supports switching source pages.
- **Improved layout visualization:** Merged paragraphs, lists, and tables can reference multiple source regions, with connecting lines to help inspect reading order, content ownership, and cross-page merges.
- **Result outline navigation:** A collapsible heading outline provides quick access to document sections.
- **Redesigned uploads and controls:** File selection, drag and drop, paste, file types, upload progress, and cancellation share one upload area. Compact tier and page-range controls improve selection and dragging, while showing the parsing service's CPU/GPU state.
- **Faster PDF previews and exports:** Preview local PDFs directly in the browser while uploading, preserve the mounted viewer and zoom after parsing, and overlay layout annotations. Reuse prepared inputs, semantic results, and assets to avoid repeated PDF and preview generation.

### PDF, formula, and table parsing

- **Improved inline formulas:** Standard/Advanced use VLM recognition for inline formula regions outside tables in the native PDF text path, retaining local formula recognition when the result is empty or invalid.
- **Footnote formulas and page-edge regions:** Preserve formula identity and reduce incorrect ownership between formulas, numbers, and body text.
- **Nested and overlapping regions:** Reduce duplicate text and excessive merging, correct annotations inside figures, and improve the reading order of merged images.
- **Consistent layout detection:** Restore per-class output thresholds in both ONNX and Torch.
- **Native text recovery:** Improve character recovery with empty ToUnicode maps and remove residual Unicode private-use characters after post-OCR processing and fallback restoration.
- **Sheared body text:** Preserve normal body text when every character in a line has a shear transformation.
- **Rotated tables:** Account for page rotation when interpreting native text orientation.
- **Atomic table content:** Keep images and formulas intact during table reconstruction rather than splitting them across cells.
- **Cross-page tables:** Preserve text boundaries between joined cells and improve blank continuations, sparse blank rows, and shared row spans.

### Native document parsing

- **Tagged PDF semantics:** Flash native PDF text parsing can use Tagged PDF/PDF/UA structure and reading order, with geometric rules handling uncovered or untrusted content.
- **Paragraph continuation:** Use indentation, sentence endings, and other page evidence to improve uppercase-leading continuations and paragraph merging across pages and columns.
- **Native tables:** Correct row segmentation affected by unusual glyph bounds and row-span ownership in some numeric tables.
- **Font weight:** Improve embedded-font weight interpretation to reduce normal body text incorrectly marked as bold.
- **Office images:** Use placeholders for some images exceeding processing limits so that one image does not fail the whole document.

### Device selection, tier recommendations, and diagnostics

- **Shared process device selection:** Model loading, automatic tier recommendations, and llama.cpp automatic mode reuse the selected runtime device, reducing duplicate probes and differences between entry points.
- **Multiple GPUs:** Match Windows GPU and memory information by physical PCI address.
- **Automatic tiers:** Recommend tiers from the actual small-model device. GPUs can enable all tiers; CPUs enable Basic from 4 available logical cores and Standard from 12.
- **ONNX discrete-GPU selection:** Windows/Linux automatic mode checks total dedicated memory. Direct GPU selection requires a capacity that rounds to at least 6 GiB; insufficient or unconfirmed capacity uses the CPU.
- **Runtime state:** Service health can report initialized CPU/GPU state without triggering device selection.
- **Faster diagnostics and CLI startup:** Run isolated runtime probes concurrently, stream reports by section, standardize capacity and device summaries, and retain full diagnostics and candidate reasons in JSON. Help and version commands load their entry points on demand.
- **Cleaner shutdown:** Improve VLM shutdown and resource release.

### Router and APIs

- **Dynamic upstream management:** Query, register, and remove remote parsing nodes without restarting the Router.
- **Graceful removal:** Stop assigning new work, then wait for existing tasks, transfers, and result references to finish.
- **Router cascading:** Connect a downstream Router as an upstream using the existing V1 protocol and result leases.
- **Separate administration credentials:** Authenticate dynamic node management independently from parsing requests.
- **Paths and filenames:** Correct CLI detection of relative and hidden-file paths, and consistently reject path-like filenames and control characters in Tasks, Router, and synchronous uploads.

### Model downloads and cache validation

- **File manifests:** Record expected files and sizes for repository, directory, and single-file resources; detect missing or truncated files, broken links, and invalid manifests before reuse.
- **Offline reuse and incremental repair:** Validate normal caches without network access or hashing large weights. Repair missing or incorrectly sized files while reusing valid files.
- **Legacy completion markers:** Continue offline reuse after required-file and shard checks. When online, verify remote metadata for the recorded revision and upgrade manifests without updating model weights.

### Local authentication and input security

- **Persistent Doclib bearer tokens:** SDK default local discovery reads credentials automatically; direct HTTP calls require a valid token.
- **Credential protection:** Set and verify POSIX private permissions and macOS/Windows ACLs.
- **URL SSRF protection:** Validate all resolved addresses and connect to a validated public IP, rejecting private, loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, and other special addresses.
- **Direct URL downloads:** Do not follow redirects or use HTTP/HTTPS/ALL proxy environment settings.
- **Document resource limits:** Stop decompression or structural expansion beyond configured budgets, including OOXML archives and XLSX merged ranges. Return a clear `resource_limit` error and preserve per-file Tasks failures.

### Upgrade notes

- Direct Doclib HTTP clients must provide a bearer token. Default SDK discovery reads it automatically; explicit service addresses or socket paths require an explicit token.
- Deployments using private URLs, redirects, or environment proxies for input downloads must adjust their input workflow. Upload private documents through the client.
- Restart the relevant process after changing device configuration. Runtime device selection stays stable within a process; the new ONNX memory threshold applies only to automatic mode.
- Minimum dependencies are **DocVortex 0.6.21** and **ModelScope 1.39.1**.

Upgrade / 升级：`pip install -U "mineru==4.2.0"`

Full changes: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/compare/mineru-4.1.0-released...mineru-4.2.0-released

name: graphify 0.9.105
body:
## graphify 0.9.105

- Fix: **watch** ignored directories (`node_modules`, `.git`, build output) are pruned from the Linux watch tree, so a large project no longer registers tens of thousands of wasted inotify watches and risks `ENOSPC`; the non-Linux recursive watcher is unchanged and still fires on every real change (#5074, #5091, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **cpp** a member-call chain routed through class fields declared in other headers (`client.actions->Execute()`, with value `.`, raw-pointer `->` and single-arg `unique_ptr`/`shared_ptr` receivers) resolves to the field type's member across the include set, gated to a unique type and member and fail-closed otherwise; a typed local whose class is in another repo is parked for the cross-repo merge (#5098, thanks @xRedLeader).
- Fix: **markdown** a code span naming an uppercase `\`-namespace class (`\Foo\Bar`, `App\API`) or a type-qualified method call (`Type::member()`) is kept as a symbol mention instead of being dropped, while a non-call `Type::CONST`/`Type::class` stays dropped (#5093, thanks @Adityakk9031).
- Fix: **ts/js** a call through a destructured CommonJS barrel require (`const { Thing } = require('./barrel')` where the barrel re-exports `Thing`) resolves to the real declaration by following the barrel's exports, instead of dropping the edge (#5034, #5104, thanks @qq2514568380).
- Fix: **wiki** the orphan sweep folds slugs with `casefold` (not `lower`), so two article names that collide only under full Unicode case-folding (`Straße`/`STRASSE`, `Σ`/`ς`) each keep their own file instead of one being deleted as an orphan; a file written this run is never swept (#5087, #5102, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **build** hyperedges are kept whole across an incremental `graphify update`: they are read from the nested graph slot a JSON-only writer uses, and after a deleted-source prune a hyperedge drops only its removed members (and itself only when none remain), instead of silently losing or leaving dangling hyperedges (#5081, #5103, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **cache** a degraded (under-producing) semantic cache entry no longer pins the corpus: after the shrink guard sees a re-extraction come back smaller than the stored graph, the entry is stamped `partial` so the next run re-dispatches it instead of replaying the degraded result forever (#5083, #5101, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **affected** `graphify affected <file>` seeds the file's nested member nodes (a method inside a class) transitively, not just one hop, so impact analysis no longer under-reports callers that bind to a nested member (#5094, thanks @Adityakk9031).
- Fix: **tree** `build_tree` derives the common directory root from file parents, so a single-file or single-directory tree is no longer self-nested under the file itself (#5092, thanks @Adityakk9031).
- Fix: **query** a label whose name is behind a schema or namespace qualifier (`public.sweep_widget_state()`, `fmt.Println`) is matched on its tail by the whole query and ranked above the per-token tiers, so it is no longer out-competed by single-token collision nodes and dropped from the seeds (#5080, #5095, thanks @sunhouy).
- Fix: **detect** an incremental staleness check hashes a file whose stamp lands within the clock-skew window on either side of its mtime, so a same-tick rewrite that does not move mtime is still caught instead of being served stale (#5090, thanks @sunhouy).
- Fix: **path** `graphify path A B` refuses an endpoint whose words appear nowhere in the graph (exit not-found) instead of returning a misleading route built from loosely-overlapping tokens (#5085, thanks @sunhouy).

- Fix: **csharp** a classic extension-method call (`x.Foo()` where `Foo` is declared `static ... Foo(this X x, ...)`) binds to the extension method's declaration through an additive pass that runs after nominal dispatch, gated to a visible namespace, a matching `this` type and a unique applicable method; an instance method of the same name wins, a non-extension static or an unimported extension gets no edge, and ambiguity fails closed (#4828, #4849, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **markdown** a bare, unqualified free-function mention in prose (`token`, no `()` and no namespace) binds to a same-named function only when its defining file (or another symbol from it) is cited within the heading's section chain, instead of matching any same-named callable in the corpus; reference-style links (`[text][label]`) resolve at the use site (#4804, #4806, thanks @madanlalit).
- Fix: **export** the `to_json` shrink guard no longer counts semantic sources that were replaced on re-extract or pruned as deletions as "lost", so a legitimate `graphify update` is not refused; a genuine unexplained shrink is still refused (#5107, thanks @khkar).
- Fix: **build** a node whose `file_type` or `confidence` arrives as a structured value (list/dict) from a drifting LLM pass no longer crashes the validate/build membership checks: validation surfaces it as a schema error, and the build folds it to `concept`/`INFERRED` without fabricating a score (#5088, thanks @sdivyanshu90).
- Fix: **llm** a splittable document below the character cap whose model output truncates is promoted to a full-range slice and bisected (and retried) instead of being kept as a truncated partial result; a non-splittable or code/binary unit still fails closed (#5072, #5078, thanks @aadilrizwan).
- Feat: **llm** a custom OpenAI-compatible provider's `extra_headers` are forwarded to the client as `default_headers`, scoped to that provider and with any `Authorization` header dropped so it cannot override the configured credential (#3680, #4783, thanks @jaimemartinez).
- Perf: **extract** whole-graph intermediates (the parse memo on the one-shot CLI, build/cluster/export working lists) are freed as soon as they are consumed, cutting peak memory on a large corpus; graph output is byte-identical (#5063, thanks @TPAteeq).
- Fix: **skillgen** the claw/kiro/pi subagent prompt now tells the worker to write its chunk to `CHUNK_PATH`, so a disk-dispatch chunk is no longer returned inline and lost at the merge step (#5040, thanks @connhodendatabase).
- Fix: **deps** the pypdf floor is raised to 6.21.4 in the `pdf` and `all` extras to pick up its security fixes (#5015, thanks @yotamleo).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 42; warm caches re-run the affected C++, Markdown and C# extractions.

name: Skill 4.8.2
body:
- **Outages named, not blamed on you.** When GitHub or impeccable.style answers a download with a server error, `install` and `update` say whose outage it is and point to its status page. They no longer suggest updating the CLI, which could not help. Thanks to @ismaelthesilva and @MihalKazi for the reports.

- **Images through your own endpoint.** `generate-image` reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, the variable the OpenAI SDKs use, so it works behind a proxy or with a compatible gateway.

- **Agent setup with a clean undo.** `impeccable agents` adds hooks, MCP servers and instruction blocks to Claude Code and Codex, removes only what it added, and leaves anything you changed alone. `impeccable agents list` reports each setup and its state.

- **Outages named.** A server error from GitHub or impeccable.style during `install` or `update` says whose outage it is and where to check its status. Nothing is installed, and your existing skills stay as they are.

- **Images through your own endpoint.** `generate-image` honors `OPENAI_BASE_URL`.

- **The current engine.** Engine 0.1.21 brings `impeccable agents` and the fixes in skill v4.8.2.
